evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you have any questions or concerns that you'd like answered on this call possibly in regards to timing the move, any specific piece of furniture.' — asked before any logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer pushed back on the estimate hours citing a shorter drive and single-story origin; rep worked through the math live, landing on 5.5-6.5 hrs, and later fully resolved the planter-waiver and propane-grill questions at the close of the call.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'You only pay for the time that we are there. So if it takes two hours, two and a half hours, you know, you only pay for the two and a half hours.'

top_strength: Exceptional real-time collaborative estimate-building with a detail-oriented repeat customer — walked through his pushback point by point and landed on a mutually credible number instead of just defending the system quote.
coaching_note: On-Time Guarantee was never mentioned anywhere in a 16-minute call — this is the one differentiator gap in an otherwise very strong call, and it's a quick, memorized line worth adding even when the conversation is running long.
grading_notes: No unusual judgment calls beyond consistent overlap-crediting of the estimate-window/proration lines under Save Your Ass, applied the same way as in other calls in this batch. Total (78) lands just short of the 80 pass bar, driven mainly by the missing quid pro quo framing, the missing On-Time Guarantee, and a soft rate-lock line at close.
